title: Intel Optane in a LAPTOP - Side-by-Side Speed Test! | The Tech Chap
description: Intel Optane Memory in Laptops gives slow mechanical hard disks fast and responsive SSD-like speeds! I'm testing ASUS laptops with and without Optane side-by-side to find out the real world speed difference*! ASUS Vivobook Pro: https://amzn.to/2Q50aVU | TUF Gaming: https://amzn.to/2Nd7Y9G  *These tests and results may vary depending on the laptop and application you use.  *This video was made in partnership with ASUS & Intel  Help support the channel when shopping on Amazon US: http://amzn.to/2qSHDlp | Amazon UK: http://amzn.to/2qg29NZ  ~ Don't forget to Subscribe & Follow me: Twitter: https://twitter.com/TheTechChap Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/TheTechChap Facebook: http://www.facebook.com/TheTechChap  ~ My Video Gear Panasonic Lumix GH5 --- US: http://amzn.to/2oQU28s | UK: http://amzn.to/2r0of6h Sigma 18-35 (w/ Metabones) ---- US: http://amzn.to/2oQVGGW | UK: http://amzn.to/2oQVUOw Sennheiser ME2 --- US: http://amzn.to/2oR4xIQ | UK: http://amzn.to/2ob8SYA Zoom H1 Recorder --- US: http://amzn.to/2obehir | UK: http://amzn.to/2oXLBqo Dell XPS 15 --- US: http://amzn.to/2oQQhjo | UK: http://amzn.to/2plsdXm

asr.full_text: Hey guys, I'm Tom the TechChap and I'm in Asus's beautiful studio set-up just outside London and I've got two of the first generation of Intel Optane laptops. We've got two VivoBook Pros here. One with Optane, one without and two of Asus's TUF gaming laptops. Again, one with Optane and one without. And I'm going to find out today just what the real-world difference is between having Optane in your system and not having it to see if it's really worthwhile. So how do you actually know if the laptop you're going to go out and buy has Intel Optane memory? Well Intel have created a whole new brand. We're looking at i5 Plus, i7 Plus and i9 Plus. This indicates these are performance processors but also coupled with Intel Optane memory. So on this Vivobook Pro we've got the core i7 plus sticker here, which tells me it's a high-performing processor and it has Optane. But as well as that, hopefully vendors and retailers will put their own stickers in the laptops, letting you know if it has it. Let's say you go into a store and you want to buy a new gaming laptop like this Asus TUF gaming laptop. If you're a gamer, you've got a massive Steam library, you're gonna want a hard drive that has a big capacity. Let's say a terabyte like this one does. But if you were to get a gaming laptop like this with a one-terabyte SSD, that would be ludicrously expensive. So for laptops like this to still be relatively affordable, something we can all go out and buy, they've stuck with a mechanical hard disk which traditionally are very slow, just loading up files, boot times, are pretty rubbish. But putting an Optane stick in here, means that while we still have a one terabyte capacity, loads and loads of room, it feels as fast as an SSD. So let's get down to it. Let me show you some side-by-side comparisons. Starting with the TUF gaming laptops. The one on the left has Intel Optane and the one on the right does not. But they do have the same 1TB hard disk. And let's start with a boot test and reaching the desktop takes 13 seconds on the laptop with Optane versus 20 seconds on the one without, but let's jump into a game. I've got Rise of the Tomb Raider here, and let's see how long it takes to get to the main menu. Not a big difference here then, 14 seconds with Optane and 16 seconds without. It is worth remembering though that, Optane isn't going to boost your frame rate or get you better performance in games. What it's doing is caching the most used apps and files, which means they can be accessed more quickly off the hard disk, making the laptop feel quicker quicker But it's not going to make a difference too You FPS in games that comes down to the graphics card the processor and your RAM now Let's move on to Pub G an infamously inefficient and sluggish game to load on any computer Really, so let's see how these two fare So it takes 52 seconds to load on the laptop with obtain and a whopping one minute and 20 on the one without it That's an extra 30 seconds to load on a laptop with Optane and a whopping one minute and 20 on the one without it. That's an extra 30 seconds to load. But of course, it's not all about gaming, so I've also got these two Vivobook Pro laptops. And again, let's start with a boot test. Once again, the laptop on the left has Optane and the one on the right does not. And it takes 16 seconds to reach the desktop with Optane versus 42 seconds on the one without it. Now these VivoBook Pros are kind of aimed at the creators and designers so it will be interesting to see how the Adobe Suite compares with Optane. So let's start with Photoshop which takes 41 seconds on the one with Optane and 1 minute and 6 on the one without. If this is your main work program and you're using it all through the day that time saved is going to add up but just wait until you see Premiere Pro which takes 24 seconds on the one the left with Optane and one minute and 54 seconds on the one without there is a ridiculous difference and of course it's not just about loading these programs faster Optane laptops will just feel more responsive on the desktop opening up folders and going to the settings menu. Just everyday desktop stuff will feel quicker and the more you use it and the more reboots it goes through, it'll get even quicker. Those speed differences between a normal hard drive and a Optane accelerated hard drive as you just saw are ridiculous. I didn't expect anything quite like that. So what that means is as I say, is that you can still go into a store or online, buy a laptop with a big capacity hard drive, plenty of room for your games or your movies or your files, whatever it is you do have on your laptop and yet you can still get that SSD speed or at least some responsiveness. So essentially, you no longer have to choose between storage capacity, the size of your hard drive and speed. It's kind of the best of both worlds. So essentially, you no longer have to choose between storage capacity , it's kind of the best of both worlds. And the best thing is, it doesn't really add to the price. When it comes to RRPs, we're looking at about £100 premium for a laptop with Optane versus one that doesn't. But after the promotions and discounts, and whatever the retailer is doing, usually you guys will probably only see a £20-£30 price difference. Not much at all for a much much faster laptop. So if you want to find out more about Intel Optane memory or any of these laptops I'll put links in the description below. A big thanks to ASUS and Intel for partnering with me on this video and I do recommend going check out these Optane laptops. If you're looking for a new one, because, well, they make a hell of a difference! Thank you so much for watching, guys. Do let me know what you make of Optane in the comments below, and do click that like and subscribe button if you want to see more of my videos. I'll see you next time, right here on the Tech Chat. Taking these home with me. See ya!
